# Dock rail previews contain long titles and read as floating panes

## Context

Merged PR #18019 made the rail reveal header use real tab-header primitives. On current `dev`, an operator-captured Workstation reveal exposed two regressions in the complete preview surface:

1. `Dependency Graph Explorer` overflows the narrow left reveal header and visually collides with chrome outside the preview.
2. A bottom reveal is shallow and visually merges with the pane underneath: the reveal root has neither an opaque surface nor elevation, so the covered header remains legible through it.

Live inspection on 2026-09-01 found the title button resolving `flex: 0 1 auto`, `white-space: nowrap`, `overflow: visible`, and `text-overflow: clip`. Its VDOM contains the long title. The existing tab system already owns the correct over-wide active-tab treatment in `.neo-tab-overflow-capped`; the reveal composition simply does not opt into it.

Memory prior art: session `8c150fe3-e8a4-4475-8694-a6f92115dce9` established that overlap defects require real rect-intersection/containment evidence, not crop-only or scroll-width probes.

## The Problem

The preview is an edge-anchored overlay by design, but it does not read as one:

- Its active-tab title can paint outside its flex allocation.
- Its root is transparent and has no box shadow, so an underlying tab header bleeds into the reveal header.
- Its free dimension comes from the last committed owning edge-zone `extent`; only an absent extent falls back to `defaultRevealFraction` (25%). A previously narrow dock band therefore creates a narrow reveal with no usability floor.

The three symptoms compound: a small, transparent, unelevated pane with escaping text reads as accidental overlap rather than a deliberate transient preview.

## The Architectural Reality

- `src/dashboard/dock/interaction/RevealOverlay.mjs` owns transient composition, visibility, and free-dimension sizing.
- `src/dashboard/dock/projection/LayoutAdapter.mjs#resolveRevealExtent()` correctly reads only the owning edge descriptor; nested split shares are not preview-size authority.
- `resources/scss/src/tab/header/Button.scss` already owns the active-tab ellipsis contract through `.neo-tab-overflow-capped`.
- `resources/scss/src/dashboard/Container.scss` owns engine reveal structure; `resources/scss/src/apps/workstation/Workspace.scss` owns Workstation-specific visual values.
- A reveal is non-modal hover/focus chrome. A workspace-wide dimmer would overstate modality and flash on pointer dwell, so this leaf uses surface opacity and elevation instead.

Decision Record impact: none; aligned with the transient overlay model in ADR 0029.

## The Fix

1. Mark the reveal title button with the existing tab overflow-cap variant. Do not duplicate the ellipsis CSS.
2. Treat `defaultRevealFraction` as both fallback and minimum: `effective = max(committedExtent, defaultRevealFraction)`. Preserve larger committed extents exactly.
3. Let Workstation supply `defaultRevealFraction: 0.35` through its existing `getDockProjectionOptions()` hook; generic consumers retain the engine default.
4. Add tokenized physical floors capped by the available workspace. Workstation supplies 20rem inline / 16rem block so a phone-width viewport does not turn 35% into a 147px pane.
5. Give the reveal root an opaque engine surface plus tokenized border/shadow; Workstation supplies its signal-aware values. Keep the overlay pointer model unchanged and add no full-workspace scrim.
6. Add full-surface visual/geometry coverage using a deliberately long title and a narrow committed extent. Assertions must include overlay boundaries and the covered neighboring header, not only the title row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A long reveal title stays within the title button and ellipsizes; its rendered rect never intersects the pin action or escapes the reveal header.
- [ ] The pin action remains fully contained and clickable at the narrowest supported reveal width.
- [ ] A committed extent below the configured default reveals at the configured floor; a larger committed extent is preserved.
- [ ] Workstation rail previews use a 35% minimum/fallback fraction plus 20rem inline / 16rem block physical floors, capped by available workspace.
- [ ] The reveal root is opaque: covered pane/header text is not visible through it.
- [ ] All four edges render a clear border/elevation boundary in Workstation dark and light palettes without a workspace-wide dimmer.
- [ ] Unit coverage pins fraction resolution and title composition; real-browser coverage pins title/pin containment and complete-preview paint.
- [ ] Exact-head unit/components CI is green.

## Out of Scope

- Changing committed dock-zone extents or relaying out the workspace during reveal.
- Adding modal pointer capture or a full-workspace backdrop/dimmer.
- Replacing the tab-header primitives introduced by #18019.

## Avoided Traps

- A title-only screenshot can pass while the complete preview escapes its boundary; assert rect containment and capture the entire overlay against neighboring content.
- New reveal-specific ellipsis rules would duplicate `.neo-tab-overflow-capped`.
- Borrowing nested split sizes would violate the owning edge-descriptor contract.
